title: The Lease Break
primary_metric: Effective cost per month actually lived in the unit, under both a "stay full term" and a "break early" scenario

options.A: Sign The Cedarline — lower monthly rent, a large non-refundable move-in fee, and a steep early-termination penalty
options.B: Sign The Aldergate — slightly higher monthly rent, a smaller security deposit, and a lease that can be broken early for one month's rent

reinforcement_note: Checked the full standards_spine.json for any n==0 skill this case's actual math (percent, ratio, proportion, decimal arithmetic, comparison) could honestly claim. As of 2026-09-03, only six skills in the entire spine have n==0: number-sense-depth, number-sense-digit, geometry-how-to-find-the-volume-of-a-sphere, calculus-how-to-use-the-quotient-rule-to-differentiate-a-quotient-of-functions, calculus-taylor-series, and calculus-how-to-find-the-taylor-series-of-a-function-at-a-point -- none of which this case's deliverables force. new_coverage[] is therefore empty. This is a deviation from the concept sheet, which framed advanced-numbers-how-to-find-a-whole-given-the-percent-and-the-part-of-the-whole as a skill this case 'would close' -- that skill's live n is 2 (covered_by two existing cases), not 0, so claiming it here would be exactly the false-positive the case-write skill warns against ('the worst case -- it silently marks a gap closed that the student never touched'). The case still closes the *topic* gap the concept sheet identified (no existing case walks through lease-signing/lease-breaking mechanics; rent-vs-own is rent-vs-buy-a-house, not lease terms) and genuinely reinforces measurement-proportion (n=17) and measurement-ratio (n=25) as the concept sheet intended, plus the percent/decimal/comparison skills the deliverables actually force.

deliverables.text: A lease-terms comparison table: monthly rent, up-front move-in cost (fee or deposit), lease term length, and early-termination terms, for The Cedarline and The Aldergate side by side.
A "stay full term" effective-monthly-cost calculation for each lease: amortize the up-front move-in cost across the full lease term and add it to monthly rent.
A "break at month 6" effective-monthly-cost calculation for each lease: amortize the up-front move-in cost and the early-termination penalty across only the months actually lived there.

A deposit-and-total-cost percent table: each lease's up-front cost as a percent of one month's rent, and each scenario's total cost as a percent of a full year of stated monthly rent, showing arithmetic in both directions (percent of a number; whole given a percent and a part).
A recommendation memo stating which lease Maya should sign, defended with D2's and D3's effective-monthly-cost numbers under both scenarios, naming why a sticker-price-only comparison would be wrong.

balance.argument_a: The Cedarline wins the stay-full-term scenario. Stay-full-term (D2): Cedarline $1,483.17 (rent $1,447 plus the $434 move-in fee amortized over 12 months) vs. Aldergate $1,734.42 (rent $1,601 plus the $1,601 deposit amortized over 12 months) -- Cedarline cheaper by 16.9%. Over a full 12-month term, The Cedarline's much lower base rent and modest move-in fee outweigh The Aldergate's smaller per-month deposit burden, because the 12-month amortization window dilutes both leases' up-front costs to only a few dollars or tens of dollars a month.
balance.argument_b: The Aldergate wins the break-at-month-6 scenario. Break-at-month-6 (D3): Cedarline $2,363.50 (rent $1,447 plus the $434 fee and $5,065 penalty amortized over 6 months) vs. Aldergate $2,134.67 (rent $1,601 plus the $1,601 deposit and $1,601 buyout amortized over 6 months) -- Aldergate cheaper by 10.7%. Halving the amortization window to 6 months roughly doubles the drag from each lease's one-time costs, and The Cedarline's termination penalty (MA2, 3.5 months' rent -- see sources S7/S8, which document a real 3-4 month range specifically for leases with several months still remaining, exactly Maya's situation) is now large enough that it outweighs The Cedarline's ongoing rent advantage. The Aldergate's capped, one-month buyout keeps its break-scenario total lower even though its full-term total is higher.
balance.margin_basis: Once Appendices A-C are sourced, compute each lease's effective monthly cost under both the stay-full-term (D2) and break-at-month-6 (D3) scenarios; margin_pct is the percentage gap between the two leases within each scenario, computed separately per scenario since the two scenarios are designed to plausibly favor different options. Target 8-12% per the concept sheet, within SPEC §2's ~20% cap.
balance.margin_pct_note: tier1_structural.py's T1-09/T1-14 checks require margin_pct to be a single scalar; this case genuinely has two scenario margins (see margin_pct_by_scenario below) because D2/D3 are designed to favor different options. Per case-qa convention (2026-09-03, reaffirmed 2026-09-04), the top-level/balance.margin_pct scalar reports the more conservative (narrower) of the two scenario margins -- break_at_month_6 = 10.7% -- since a narrower margin is the more binding constraint against SPEC §2's ~20% cap. The wider stay_full_term margin (16.9%) is preserved in full below and remains flagged as a GAP (inside the cap but wide -- discussion will lean one-sided in that half).

margin_pct_by_scenario.note: RETUNED 2026-09-04 (case-readiness remediation, re-entering at case-write/case-research per PIPELINE.md's 'QA BLOCKER on balance -> re-enter at case-write'): the previous pass (2026-09-03) found Cedarline cheaper in BOTH scenarios (16.9% and 6.6%), meaning the dilemma did not flip as designed. Root cause: MA2 (Cedarline's termination penalty) was set at 2 months' rent, the top of the ordinary 1-2 month range [S5] but not large enough for The Cedarline's ongoing rent advantage to be overcome even at month 6. Fix: two new real sources (S7, S8) independently document that early-termination fees run 2-4 (S7) or specifically 3-4 (S8) months' rent when, as in Maya's break-at-month-6 scenario, several months remain on the lease -- a real, sourced, scenario-matched basis distinct from the ordinary range. MA2 was revised to 3.5 months' rent. SEPARATELY, a later Tier 2 P6 data-decay check (2026-09-04) found S1/S2's live rent-trends page had moved on from its originally-cited $1,389/$1,536 figures to $1,447/$1,601 -- S1/S2 and every figure derived from them as a percent/multiple (MA1, MA2, MA3, MA4, MA9) were refreshed accordingly. Recomputed with current figures: stay-full-term still favors Cedarline (16.9%, essentially unchanged since both rents moved together), and break-at-month-6 now genuinely favors Aldergate (10.7%, within the concept sheet's 8-12% target band and SPEC §2's ~20% cap). The dilemma now flips exactly as the concept sheet and original case design intended, with every figure real, cited, current, and non-fabricated -- no number was hidden or the margin fixed by omission, per PIPELINE.md's 'never fix a margin by hiding data.'

modeling_assumptions.basis: Redfin reports typical non-refundable move-in fees at 20-50% of monthly rent [S3]; case picks ~30% (upper-middle of the range) to embody the 'large' fee the narrative describes. REVISED 2026-09-04 alongside S1's refresh: 30% of the current $1,447 rent = $434 (was $415 at the prior $1,389 rent).
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Amortized over 12 months (D2), a few dollars/month either way -- not dilemma-flipping on its own.

modeling_assumptions.basis: REVISED 2026-09-04 (case-readiness remediation, see sensitivity_note): the general 1-2 months' rent range [S5] grounds the ordinary case, but two independent sources -- Landing [S7], general range 2-4 months' rent, and a second, distinct LeaseRunner article [S8] -- both report the real range widens specifically when 'several months remain on the lease' at the time of the break. Maya's break-at-month-6 scenario (6 of the Cedarline's 12-month term still outstanding) is exactly that case. The case picks 3.5 months' rent, the middle of S8's stated 3-4 month elevated sub-range, rather than the ordinary range that would apply to a lease nearly at its end anyway.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Highest-leverage assumption in the case, and now the assumption that restores the case's intended scenario-dependent reversal (see balance.margin_pct_by_scenario). It is the largest line item in The Cedarline's break-at-month-6 total (D3); a Hero arguing for a milder penalty within the ordinary 1-2 month range [S5] is making a legitimate challenge and should show how far the number would have to move before the recommendation flips back.

modeling_assumptions.basis: One month's rent is the dominant private-market security-deposit convention nationally, corroborated by HUD's public-housing deposit cap [S6] and widely mirrored in state landlord-tenant statutes; matches the narrative's description of a 'smaller, more conventional' deposit. REVISED 2026-09-04 alongside S2's refresh: 1 month of the current $1,601 rent (was $1,536 at the prior $1,536 rent).
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Low -- refundable, so it moves D2/D3 totals by a small, fixed amount in both scenarios.

modeling_assumptions.basis: LeaseRunner-cited real range of 1-2 months' rent for termination buyouts [S5]; case states the Aldergate's clause at the bottom (most tenant-favorable) end, matching the narrative's 'stated buyout of one month's rent.' REVISED 2026-09-04 alongside S2's refresh: 1 month of the current $1,601 rent (was $1,536).
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Moderate -- this is what keeps The Aldergate's early-exit cost capped and predictable rather than open-ended.

modeling_assumptions.basis: Fixed-term QA/contract-testing engagements commonly run in 3/6/12-month increments; 6 months is a plausible mid-length engagement, short enough that an early lease break is a real risk.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Sets up MA6; lengthening toward 12 months would remove the break-early scenario entirely.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: If Maya's contract extends, the length of that extension
modeling_assumptions.value: Covers the remainder of the signed lease's full 12-month term
modeling_assumptions.basis: Added 2026-09-04 (case-readiness Tier 2 P4 remediation): the case only models two scenarios (D2 stay-full-term, D3 break-at-month-6), matching the Background's binary framing ('if it extends, she stays put for the long haul'). This assumption states explicitly what that framing implies but had never been written as its own figure -- without it, a student could ask 'what if the extension is only a few months?', a case the appendices do not model, which a Tier 2 twist-integrity probe correctly flagged as an unstated convention the discussion's Twist otherwise silently depended on.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: None directly -- a scoping convention, not a number in D2-D4's arithmetic. It matters only for the Twist's clean mapping of 'extended' to D2 and 'not extended' to D3.

sensitivity_note: RESOLVED 2026-09-04 (case-readiness remediation, re-entered at case-write/case-research per PIPELINE.md's 'QA BLOCKER on balance -> re-enter at case-write'), with a second remediation the same day after a Tier 2 P6 data-decay check. Prior finding (case-qa, 2026-09-03): with the then-current sourced/assumed figures, The Cedarline was cheaper in BOTH computed scenarios (16.9% stay-full-term, 6.6% break-at-month-6), so the case's central premise -- that the two scenarios plausibly favor different options -- did not hold. Investigation found that MA2 (Cedarline's termination penalty) could not be raised past its previously-cited real range (1-2 months' rent, S5) far enough to flip the break-at-month-6 scenario without an unsupported assumption. Further real-world research found two additional, independent real sources -- S7 (Landing, 2-4 months' rent general range) and S8 (a second, distinct LeaseRunner article, 1-2 months typical but 3-4 months 'in tight markets or when several months remain on the lease') -- documenting a real, higher range specifically applicable to Maya's exact situation: breaking a 12-month lease with 6 months (half the term) still remaining. MA2 was revised to 3.5 months' rent. SEPARATELY (same day), Tier 2 probe 5 (twist-integrity) found the discussion Twist's mapping of 'extension confirmed/not confirmed' onto the D2/D3 scenarios relied on an unstated convention (how long an extension runs) -- fixed by adding MA10, stating explicitly that an extension, if granted, covers the remainder of the lease's 12-month term. AND Tier 2 probe 6 (data decay) found S1/S2's live rent-trends page had moved on from its originally-cited $1,389/$1,536 figures (as of 2026-07-02) to $1,447/$1,601 (as of 2026-08-31) -- S1/S2 and every figure derived from them as a percent/multiple (MA1, MA2, MA3, MA4, MA9) were refreshed to the current values. Recomputed with all current figures: stay-full-term margin is 16.9% (Cedarline; essentially unchanged since both units' rents moved together), and break-at-month-6 now genuinely favors The Aldergate by 10.7% -- within the concept sheet's 8-12% target band and SPEC §2's ~20% cap. The dilemma now flips exactly as the concept sheet and original case design intended. No figure was fabricated or hidden to force this result: every value is real, currently-cited, and its basis and every revision are recorded here, in RESEARCH_LOG.md, and in case.md's Appendix D and Modeling Assumptions block. Remaining GAP (not a blocker): the stay-full-term margin (16.9%) is wide relative to the 8-12% target, so that half of the discussion will lean one-sided toward Cedarline -- flagged for facilitators in FACILITATOR.md.

qa.note: RESOLVED 2026-09-04 (case-write/case-research remediation, two rounds; see RESEARCH_LOG.md, QA_REPORT.md, and this case's balance/sensitivity_note for full detail). Root defect: MA2 (Cedarline's termination penalty) was set within the ordinary 1-2 month range [S5], not large enough to overcome Cedarline's rent advantage even at month 6, so Cedarline won both scenarios and the designed reversal did not exist. Fixed by sourcing two new real ranges (S7, S8) specific to a lease with several months remaining and revising MA2 to 3.5 months' rent. Two further genuine defects surfaced and fixed during Tier 2 itself: an unstated extension-length convention undermining the Twist (fixed by adding MA10), and a data-decay drift in S1/S2's live rent source (fixed by refreshing S1/S2 and recomputing every dependent assumption). Final state: stay-full-term favors Cedarline by 16.9%, break-at-month-6 favors Aldergate by 10.7% -- a genuine scenario-dependent reversal, both margins real/cited/non-fabricated and within SPEC §2's ~20% cap, break-scenario margin inside the concept sheet's 8-12% target band.

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: MA2 is a stated scenario assumption for an invented apartment (The Cedarline) chosen from within a real, cited range (S5's ordinary 1-2 months' rent, S7/S8's elevated 2-4/3-4 month range for a lease with several months remaining). No real listing exists to research further -- there is no single 'true' penalty to discover, only a real-world range to choose within. At -50% (back toward the ordinary range) the verdict flips to Cedarline; at +50% the margin exceeds the 20% cap. Both directions are disclosed here, in case.json.balance and in FACILITATOR.md's sensitivity note, and are a legitimate Hero challenge point precisely because this is the case's highest-leverage dial.

MA6 (and MA5, the contract's firm term) model whether Maya's fixed-term contract extends or ends on schedule -- a genuinely unknowable-in-advance outcome that the case's own Background and FACILITATOR.md Anchor 4 name explicitly as the load-bearing uncertainty nobody, including Maya, can resolve ahead of the signing deadline. At break_month flexed to 3 (a shorter engagement than stated), the break-scenario margin widens past the SPEC §2 20% cap; at 9 months it narrows. This is disclosed here and in FACILITATOR.md; it does not change which lease wins at the case's own stated 6-month value, only how wide the margin would be under a different, equally unknowable contract length.
